reasoning_traces.think:
The Bayesian Mixture Model (BMM) constructs a smooth Expected Possession Value (EPV) surface by combining fixed weights with learned outcome probabilities at predefined centers. Each center encodes a Dirichlet-multinomial posterior over 5 possession outcomes, enabling probabilistic inference under uncertainty. The model interpolates these centers using bilinear weights over a spatial grid defined by field coordinates. This approach improves upon zonal Markov Reward Processes by offering continuous spatial variation and individual outcome probabilities. In GSI, this framework supports hierarchical team priors and robust EPV estimation even in sparse data regimes. For GSE, it enables dynamic state transitions based on continuous EPV fields, enhancing situational awareness and strategic decision-making. The method's reliance on fixed weights ensures computational efficiency while maintaining flexibility through learned center probabilities. Failure modes include boundary artifacts from interpolation and underfitting in low-action zones, which can be mitigated by adaptive weighting schemes or increased data density.
